problem: The sentence says flatly that the end device is a reduced-function device. In ZigBee a ZigBee end device may be built on either an FFD or an RFD; only the coordinator and routers must be FFDs. As written it contradicts the standard texts.
fix: In 802.15.4 terms the coordinator and routers must be full-function devices. A ZigBee end device is usually a reduced-function device, but the standard also allows an end device built on an FFD; either way it does not forward packets.

problem: "Some syllabi call these application profiles, others the ZigBee application layer" treats two different things as two names for one thing. The ZigBee application layer is the whole upper layer (APS + ZDO + application framework); an application profile is one of the documents that defines clusters such as HA or SE.
fix: An application profile is a document that fixes which clusters an application uses; the ZigBee application layer is the layer that contains APS, the ZDO and these profiles.

problem: The count of 5 parents with 6 free child slots each ignores that in ZigBee every router itself joins as a child of some parent, so it occupies one of the coordinator's (or another router's) child slots. The number 30 therefore double-counts capacity; a student who takes the example literally will get a different answer in an exam that states the routers are children of the coordinator.
fix: State the assumption used: "Count only the child slots available for end devices, assuming the 4 routers have already joined and their slots are not counted again." Then the arithmetic 5 × 6 = 30 is valid under that stated assumption.

problem: "How many end devices lose their parent?" is ambiguous. Strictly, every child of the two failed routers loses its parent; the number 2 is the number that cannot find a new parent after re-joining.
fix: Ask "After the failed routers' children try to re-join, how many end devices are left without a parent?" and keep the answer 20 − 18 = 2.
